newsitem.title: CHINA: China auto imports down in Q1, exports up.
newsitem.headline: China auto imports down in Q1, exports up.

text.p: China's automobile imports fell 18.77 percent in the first quarter of 1997, while exports climbed 9.95 percent, the Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday, quoting the Ministry of Machine-Building Industry.
Imports totalled $347 million during the period, while exports were $139 million, Xinhua said.
Imports of whole vehicles plunged 48.97 percent to 8,000 units, it said. Their value fell 32.06 percent to $120 million.
China imported 37,000 engines, down 15.11 percent, the agency said. Their value plummeted 35.85 percent to $26 million.
Import of auto parts, components and bodies slipped 3.86 percent to $190 million, it said.

During the period, China exported 2,779 heavy-duty trucks, up 53.71 percent, Xinhua said. Exports of cars and special-purpose vehicles soared 102 percent and 119 percent to 388 and 158 units respectively.
